accepted.s: The National River Conservation Plan (NRCP), launched in 1995, primarily aims to improve the water quality of which of the following?
o: Rivers other than the Ganga and its tributaries
The Ganga and all its tributaries only
Inter-State rivers exclusively through private funding
accepted.x: NRCP was launched in 1995 to improve the water quality of rivers other than the Ganga and its tributaries through a Centre-State cost-sharing Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the scope of closely related river-conservation programmes.
accepted.sec: River conservation programmes - NRCP, GRCA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following activities is supported under the National River Conservation Plan?
o: Interception and diversion of sewage, sewage treatment plants and low-cost sanitation
Construction of dams exclusively for hydropower generation
Replacement of all municipal water-supply pipelines
accepted.x: NRCP funds interception and diversion of sewage, sewage treatment plants and low-cost sanitation measures to reduce pollution loads in rivers.
accepted.tq: Identify the actual functions of the concerned programme rather than its neighbouring sectors.
accepted.sec: River conservation programmes - NRCP, GRCA  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National River Conservation Plan:
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme involving Centre-State cost sharing.
2. It covers 38 rivers in 16 States.
3. Godavari and Krishna are among the rivers included under it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. NRCP is a Centre-State cost-sharing scheme covering 38 rivers in 16 States, including the Godavari and Krishna.
accepted.tq: Use the coded combination to verify programme structure, coverage and examples.
accepted.sec: River conservation programmes - NRCP, GRCA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA) was launched at which event and place?
o: COP27 at Sharm el-Sheikh in November 2022
World Water Forum at New Delhi in 2023
accepted.x: GRCA was launched at COP28 held in Dubai in December 2023. It was not launched at New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Apply the event-place-year combination to avoid a location swap.
accepted.sec: River conservation programmes - NRCP, GRCA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which organisation leads the Global River Cities Alliance?
o: National Disaster Management Authority under the Ministry of Home Affairs
National Mission for Clean Ganga under the Ministry of Jal Shakti
NITI Aayog under the Ministry of Finance
Central Pollution Control Board under the Ministry of Environment
accepted.x: The Global River Cities Alliance is led by the National Mission for Clean Ganga under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the responsible body.
accepted.sec: River conservation programmes - NRCP, GRCA  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. GAP-I
b. GAP-II
c. NRCP
List-II (Year and scope)
i. 1985 — 25 main-stem Ganga towns
ii. 1993 — 60 towns on the Yamuna, Gomti, Damodar and Mahananda
iii. 1995 — rivers other than the Ganga

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: GAP-I began in 1985 for 25 main-stem Ganga towns; GAP-II began in 1993 for 60 towns on specified tributaries and rivers; NRCP began in 1995 for rivers other than the Ganga.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure year-scope pair and eliminate the remaining codes.
accepted.sec: River conservation programmes - NRCP, GRCA  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following programmes in chronological order of their commencement:
A. NRCP
B. GAP-II
C. GAP-I

Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: GAP-I commenced in 1985, GAP-II in 1993 and NRCP in 1995. Therefore, the correct order is C, B, A.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest years first, then place the intermediate programme.
accepted.sec: River conservation programmes - NRCP, GRCA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Singtam sewerage project on the Teesta in Sikkim has a capacity of 3 MLD, not 30 MLD, and its cost is ₹39.03 crore.
accepted.tq: Find the numerical magnitude trap among closely related project details.
accepted.sec: River conservation programmes - NRCP, GRCA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Global River Cities Alliance covers which of the following?
o: Only cities of countries sharing the Ganga basin
Only Indian cities situated on the Ganga
Only capital cities of countries participating in COP28
River cities worldwide, with partner countries, international funding agencies and knowledge partners
accepted.x: GRCA is a global alliance covering river cities worldwide and involves partner countries, international funding agencies and knowledge partners.
accepted.tq: Reject the restrictive ‘only’ options when the programme has global coverage.
accepted.sec: River conservation programmes - NRCP, GRCA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the cited CPCB report, a polluted river stretch is identified when the biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) is:
accepted.x: The cited criterion for a polluted river is BOD greater than 3 mg/L. A BOD greater than 30 mg/L identifies a Priority-I stretch.
accepted.tq: Separate the general threshold from the more severe Priority-I threshold.
accepted.sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The BOD level associated with Priority-I polluted river stretches is:
accepted.x: Priority-I polluted river stretches are those with BOD greater than 30 mg/L.
accepted.tq: Test the higher category threshold rather than the ordinary pollution cut-off.
accepted.sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding polluted river stretches in India:
1. The latest cited CPCB report identified 296 polluted stretches on 271 rivers.
2. Maharashtra had the highest number of polluted stretches, with 54.
3. The number of polluted stretches increased from 351 in 2018 to 296 in the latest cited report.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the number declined from 351 in 2018 to 296 in the latest cited report.
accepted.tq: Track the direction of change instead of accepting a reversed trend.
accepted.sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The number of polluted river stretches reported for 2022 was:
accepted.x: The cited series records 351 polluted stretches in 2018, 311 in 2022 and 296 in the latest report.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year-specific intermediate figure from the latest total.
accepted.sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the water quality index cited in NITI Aayog’s Composite Water Management Index 2018, India was ranked:
accepted.x: India was ranked 120th among 122 countries in the water quality index cited in the NITI Aayog CWMI 2018.
accepted.tq: Read the rank and denominator together; do not reverse their order.
accepted.sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the cited CGWB Annual Ground Water Quality Report, fluoride exceeded 1.5 mg/L at what percentage of the assessed sites in 2024?
accepted.x: Fluoride concentration exceeded 1.5 mg/L at 9.04% of the assessed sites in the 2024 report.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact percentage rather than approximating the reported figure.
accepted.sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the order of the States with the highest reported occurrence of fluoride above 1.5 mg/L in groundwater?
accepted.x: The reported order is Rajasthan first, followed by Haryana and Karnataka.
accepted.tq: Test a ranked comparison by preserving the order of the three entries.
accepted.sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which polluted river stretch in Andhra Pradesh was identified near Rajamahendravaram?
accepted.x: The Godavari near Rajamahendravaram was identified among the polluted river stretches in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the place-river association to avoid swapping neighbouring river systems.
accepted.sec: Water quality reports and polluted river stretches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Kolleru Lake is under severe pollution stress primarily because:
o: It receives untreated sewage from Delhi and Haryana
Its lake bed was converted into aquaculture ponds and it receives farm runoff
It is affected only by sea-water intrusion
Its water is diverted exclusively for thermal power generation
accepted.x: Kolleru’s severe eutrophication is linked to conversion of the lake bed into aquaculture ponds and the inflow of farm runoff.
accepted.tq: Link the environmental condition with its stated local causes.
accepted.sec: AP water bodies under pollution stress  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following places or activities is associated with pollution stress in Andhra Pradesh water bodies?
1. Godavari and Krishna stretches near cities
2. Effluents from Pharma City in Visakhapatnam
3. Tanneries and paper mills
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three are identified sources or locations associated with pollution stress in Andhra Pradesh water bodies.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when each listed local source is supported.
accepted.sec: AP water bodies under pollution stress  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At Rajamahendravaram, the municipal corporation discharges approximately how much sewage through the Nalla Channel before drawing drinking water downstream?
accepted.x: The municipal corporation discharges 29.6 MLD of sewage through the Nalla Channel and draws 65 MLD of drinking water just downstream.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the sewage-discharge figure from the downstream drinking-water withdrawal.
accepted.sec: AP water bodies under pollution stress  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Godavari at Rajamahendravaram:
1. The municipal corporation draws 65 MLD of drinking water downstream of the Nalla Channel discharge.
2. The river stretch was reported to be unfit for drinking or bathing.
3. Nitrate concentration was reported as 119.6 mg/L.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The reported stretch was unfit for drinking or bathing, had nitrate at 119.6 mg/L, and the city drew 65 MLD downstream of the discharge.
accepted.tq: Verify several independent measurements and use conditions together rather than relying on one figure.
accepted.sec: AP water bodies under pollution stress  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following were identified as the main polluters associated with the Godavari at Rajamahendravaram?
o: Thermal plants and urban water-supply reservoirs
Pharma City and the Krishna Delta canal
Andhra Paper Ltd. and the Nalla Channel
Only aquaculture ponds in Kolleru Lake
accepted.x: Andhra Paper Ltd. and the Nalla Channel were identified as the main polluters. The Andhra Paper Ltd. discharge was reported at 31,934 KLD.
accepted.tq: Match the water body with the locally identified polluting sources.
accepted.sec: AP water bodies under pollution stress  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What proportion of urban sewage is treated in India according to the cited estimate?
accepted.x: Only about 28% of urban sewage is treated, while about 72% is discharged untreated.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the treated share from its untreated complement.
accepted.sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a sequencing batch reactor (SBR)?
o: It is a membrane-only process designed exclusively for drinking-water desalination
It treats sewage continuously in separate tanks without biological treatment
It uses only activated carbon and no biological process
It treats sewage in batches in a single tank
accepted.x: An SBR carries out treatment in batches within one tank, integrating the sequential stages of the treatment process.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between SBR and MBR by focusing on batch operation versus membrane filtration.
accepted.sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A membrane bioreactor (MBR) is best described as a system that:
o: Stores untreated sewage until natural dilution occurs
Combines biological treatment with membrane filtration for high-quality reuse
Treats sewage through evaporation without biological treatment
Uses only coarse screening for removal of floating matter
accepted.x: An MBR combines biological treatment with membrane filtration and can produce water suitable for high-quality reuse.
accepted.tq: Use the defining technology in the term rather than confusing it with ordinary activated-sludge treatment.
accepted.sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following technologies are associated with sewage treatment plants evaluated or used in the cited context?
1. Activated sludge
2. Membrane bioreactors
3. Activated-carbon polishing
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Activated sludge, membrane bioreactors and activated-carbon polishing are all recognised sewage-treatment technologies in the cited context.
accepted.tq: Check whether each listed technology belongs to the treatment chain before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Hybrid Annuity Model for Namami Gange projects, what proportion of payments is linked to 15 years of operation and maintenance?
accepted.x: The Hybrid Annuity Model links 60% of payments to 15 years of operation and maintenance.
accepted.tq: Identify the contractual percentage and its associated time period together.
accepted.sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Hybrid Annuity Model projects under Namami Gange are intended to treat approximately:
accepted.x: The HAM projects under Namami Gange are intended to treat 6,255 MLD of sewage.
accepted.tq: Use digit placement carefully when distinguishing project capacities.
accepted.sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the urban sewage-treatment gap?
o: Piped sewerage reaches 28% of urban households, plants run at 72% capacity and 33% is treated.
Piped sewerage reaches 64% of urban households, plants run at 33% capacity and 72% is treated.
Piped sewerage reaches 72% of urban households, plants run at 28% capacity and 64% is treated.
Piped sewerage reaches 33% of urban households, plants run at 64% capacity and about 28% of urban sewage is treated.
accepted.x: The reported gap consists of piped sewerage access for only 33% of urban households, plant utilisation at 64% capacity and treatment of about 28% of urban sewage.
accepted.tq: Keep the three percentages attached to their correct indicators instead of interchanging them.
accepted.sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about AMRUT 2.0 is correct?
o: It was launched in 2022 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti and covers only river navigation.
It was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and covers sewerage and water supply.
It was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Finance and covers only industrial effluent.
It was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Environment and covers only solid waste.
accepted.x: AMRUT 2.0 was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and covers sewerage and water supply.
accepted.tq: Apply the ministry-year-subject triad to avoid swapping authorities.
accepted.sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: AMRUT 2.0 mandates reuse of what proportion of treated urban wastewater?
accepted.x: AMRUT 2.0 mandates reuse of 20% of treated urban wastewater.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the mandated reuse target from sewerage-coverage and treatment percentages.
accepted.sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the stated safe-reuse framework, thermal power plants located within what distance of a sewage treatment plant must use treated wastewater?
accepted.x: Thermal plants located within 50 km of a sewage treatment plant must use treated wastewater under the stated framework.
accepted.tq: Identify the distance threshold linked to the mandatory reuse requirement.
accepted.sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The relaxation of the BOD discharge limit from 10 mg/L to 30 mg/L was criticised primarily because it:
o: Permits a higher concentration of organic pollution in discharged effluent
Reduces the permissible BOD limit by two-thirds
Applies only to drinking-water treatment plants
Requires all effluent to contain exactly 30 mg/L of BOD
accepted.x: Raising the limit from 10 mg/L to 30 mg/L permits a higher BOD concentration in discharged effluent, which attracted criticism.
accepted.tq: Infer the environmental effect of a reversed regulatory trend—an increased permissible limit.
accepted.sec: Sewage treatment - technologies, gap, HAM, AMRUT  [APPSC]
